title: Trying out for football against 'Train' Colger
summary: He insisted on football until a 350-pound guard ran over him, and then went to the band room.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And you went there. Okay. What was it like when you first, well, showed up at 'Bama State? What, can you give us an idea of what kinds of things happened?

Well, I was still doing the Lennie's Temple. They had, the word got out about music for me there. And, I was in the gymnasium putting on football togs to go out and go for the football team. So, when I got out there, they said no. You go to the band room. I was weighing about 165 lbs., I suppose. I said no. I want to play football. And, I insisted on playing football. I said I'll go to the band room later. But, I want to play football.

But, they found out about my music. They wanted me there instead. So, they said, they showed me a guard, a fellow they called "Train". His name was Colger. He weighed about 350 lbs. They said okay. You want to play
football. They didn't have grass out on the turf like they have now. That was dirt. Rocks. They said if you can tackle him, you can stay out here to play football.

I said send him on down. You know, send him on down here. Now, I'm 165, he's 350. And I, I wondered, they called him "Train" I said. He came out with that ball in his arm. And, the closer he got me, he sounded like a locomotive. So, I braced myself to tackle him and he didn't break stride. He walked, he ran right over me and kept on going.
And, I got up, brushed myself off, just like they asked me to do and went to the gymnasium. I took my togs off and went to the band room. They didn't see me out on that football field again.
